title: 20 Beautiful Villages in Crete
seoTitle: 20 Beautiful Villages in Crete, by Region and Drive Time
seoDescription: Twenty Cretan villages worth the drive, each with its region, altitude, speciality and driving time from Rethymno, from Margarites to roadless Loutro.
summary: The twenty villages worth driving to in Crete run from Maroulas, fifteen minutes from Rethymno with its Venetian tower houses, to Mochlos on the north-east coast two and a half hours away. The essential cluster sits within 45 minutes of Rethymno: Margarites for pottery, Argyroupoli for its springs, Spili for the 25-spout lion fountain, and Anogeia at 740 m for lyra music and shepherd culture. Further afield lie Archanes in the Heraklion wine country, Zaros beneath Psiloritis, Kritsa above Agios Nikolaos for weaving and the Panagia Kera frescoes, the chestnut village of Elos, and Loutro in Sfakia, which has no road in or out at all.
body:
The coastal resorts are where Crete sells itself; the villages are where it lives. Inland, the island is a network of settlements strung along olive terraces and mountain plateaux, most of them within an hour of the north coast and almost none of them on a coach route. The twenty below are worth the drive, and each one has a specific reason to go rather than a general one.

The full list of [things to do in Crete](/en/guides/authentic-crete-experiences) is the companion to this page.

All driving times are one way from Rethymno, which is the most central base on the island. Regions are given as the prefecture the village sits in.

## All twenty, by region and drive time

| Village | Region | From Rethymno | Altitude | Known for |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Maroulas | Rethymno | 15 min | 220 m | Venetian and Ottoman tower houses |
| Margarites | Rethymno | 25 min | 300 m | Pottery, still on the wheel |
| Argyroupoli | Rethymno | 25 min | 260 m | Springs, plane trees, ancient Lappa |
| Kournas | Chania | 25 min | 220 m | Village above Crete's only freshwater lake |
| Spili | Rethymno | 30 min | 430 m | The 25-spout Venetian lion fountain |
| Vamos | Chania (Apokoronas) | 40 min | 210 m | Restored stone houses, agrotourism co-operative |
| Axos | Rethymno | 40 min | 500 m | Psiloritis foothills, Byzantine churches |
| Thronos | Rethymno (Amari) | 40 min | 500 m | Frescoed basilica over the Amari valley |
| Meronas | Rethymno (Amari) | 45 min | 400 m | Kalergi mansions, 14th-century frescoes |
| Anogeia | Rethymno | 45 min | 740 m | Lyra music, resistance history, shepherds |
| Chora Sfakion | Chania | 1 h 15 | Sea level | Gateway to the roadless south-west |
| Archanes | Heraklion | 1 h 15 | 380 m | Wine country, award-winning restoration |
| Zaros | Heraklion | 1 h 15 | 350 m | Springs, trout, Rouvas Gorge |
| Anopoli | Chania (Sfakia) | 1 h 40 | 600 m | Plateau above Loutro, Aradaina bridge |
| Milia | Chania | 2 h | 500 m | Abandoned settlement rebuilt off-grid |
| Kapetaniana | Heraklion (Asterousia) | 2 h | 750 m | Mount Kofinas, the Libyan Sea below |
| Loutro | Chania (Sfakia) | Boat from Chora Sfakion | Sea level | No road in or out |
| Elos | Chania | 2 h 15 | 550 m | Chestnut villages; festival in October |
| Kritsa | Lasithi | 2 h 15 | 375 m | Weaving, Panagia Kera frescoes |
| Mochlos | Lasithi | 2 h 30 | Sea level | Fishing village with a Minoan islet offshore |

## Rethymno region: the villages you can reach before lunch

### Maroulas — 15 minutes
The closest, and the most overlooked. Maroulas has a dozen Venetian and Ottoman tower houses, olive presses built into the rock, and a scale that makes an hour enough. Go for the architecture; stay for a coffee in the square.

### Margarites — 25 minutes
The pottery village of Crete. A dozen active studios line two narrow streets, and the potters still throw shapes that descend directly from Minoan storage jars alongside modern work. Watch a wheel, buy something that will not survive your hand luggage, and drink coffee under the plane trees looking down the valley. It is the core stop on our [Timeless Crete: Villages & Monasteries](/tours/timeless-crete-villages-monasteries) tour.

### Argyroupoli — 25 minutes
Built on ancient Lappa, and split into an upper village of Venetian doorways and a lower one where spring water pours out of the hillside under enormous plane trees, runs through channels, drives a couple of old mills and keeps the tavernas' trout alive. Ten degrees cooler than the coast in August.

### Spili — 30 minutes
A green village on the flank of Mount Kedros, built around a Venetian fountain whose twenty-five carved lion heads pour cold mountain water into a long trough. Everyone fills a bottle. The cobbled lanes above the main street are full of bougainvillea and shops selling mountain herbs and olive wood. Spili is a stop on both the [Cretan Nature & Village Journey](/tours/cretan-nature-village-journey) and the [Botanical Tours of Crete](/tours/botanical-tours-crete).

### Axos — 40 minutes
On the road up to Psiloritis, with several small Byzantine churches and a view down the Mylopotamos valley. Quiet, working, and a good place to stop between Margarites and Anogeia.

### Thronos — 40 minutes
The Amari valley is the loveliest inland region in Crete and Thronos sits at the top of it, in a basilica built on an early Christian mosaic floor, with 14th-century frescoes inside and the whole valley below. Mount Psiloritis fills the eastern horizon.

### Meronas — 45 minutes
Also in the Amari, and the seat of the Kalergi family. The church of the Panagia holds frescoes from the same century and a Venetian-influenced facade. The valley road between Thronos, Meronas and Gerakari in spring, when the cherry trees are out, is one of the best drives on the island.

### Anogeia — 45 minutes
The most singular village in Crete: 740 m up on the flank of Psiloritis, rebuilt after the Germans razed it in 1944, and the home of Cretan lyra music. The dialect preserves ancient Greek words that have vanished elsewhere. It is a shepherd town, and the mountain culture is not staged. For the working version of it, our [Shepherd for a Day](/tours/shepherd-for-a-day-crete) experience puts you in a sheepfold making cheese rather than watching someone else do it.

## Chania region

### Kournas — 25 minutes
A small village on the slope above Lake Kournas, Crete's only natural freshwater lake. Tavernas up here look down on the water; the lake itself is ten minutes below. Combined with the springs at Argyroupoli on our [Lake Kournas & Argyroupoli](/tours/lake-kournas-argyroupoli-springs-tour) half-day.

### Vamos — 40 minutes
The administrative centre of the Apokoronas, and the site of one of Greece's earliest agrotourism co-operatives: villagers restored their own stone houses in the 1990s rather than sell them. The result is a working village with rooms to rent, a good taverna and an olive-oil culture it will explain to you at length.

### Chora Sfakion — 1 hour 15
Small, austere, and the most useful village on the south coast: the ferry port for Loutro, Agia Roumeli and Marmara, and the end of the Imbros Gorge day. Sfakia has its own history of insurrection and its own cheese pies, and the harbour front tavernas do both well.

### Anopoli — 1 hour 40
A plateau village at 600 m above Loutro, with a statue of Daskalogiannis in the square and the road on to the Aradaina bridge — 138 m above the gorge, and a bungee jump if you are that way inclined. Start point for the [Aradaina Gorge](/tours/aradaina-gorge) descent.

### Milia — 2 hours
An abandoned 17th-century settlement in the western mountains, rebuilt in the 1980s as an off-grid guesthouse: solar power, stone rooms, no televisions, and food grown on the terraces below. Reached by a track through chestnut forest.

### Loutro — boat from Chora Sfakion
There is no road. Loutro is a horseshoe of white houses around a bay, reachable only by ferry or on foot along the coastal path, which means no cars, no coaches and no day-trip traffic. It is the quietest place on Crete you can sleep in.

### Elos — 2 hours 15
The heart of the chestnut villages of the far west, in deep shade under trees that are centuries old. The chestnut festival in the third week of October is the reason most people come; the rest of the year it is a green, cool, almost alpine corner of an otherwise arid island.

## Heraklion region

### Archanes — 1 hour 15
In the wine country south of Heraklion, and the best-restored village on the island — it has won European awards for it. Neoclassical facades, a large square full of good tavernas, several serious wineries within a few kilometres, and the Minoan cemetery at Phourni on the hill above.

### Zaros — 1 hour 15
At the foot of Psiloritis, built around freshwater springs that supply the island's bottled water and feed trout farms you can eat at. The Rouvas Gorge and the Byzantine monastery of Agios Nikolaos start from the lake above the village, and the walking here is among the best in central Crete.

### Kapetaniana — 2 hours
High in the Asterousia range at 750 m, looking down at the Libyan Sea. The village is the base for the climb up Mount Kofinas and for the hermitages cut into the cliffs below. Remote, sparsely inhabited, and worth the road.

## Lasithi region

### Kritsa — 2 hours 15
Built amphitheatrically up a mountainside above Agios Nikolaos, and famous for weaving: women here still work hand looms, and the textiles hanging in the lanes are made rather than imported. Just below the village, the church of Panagia Kera holds the finest surviving Byzantine frescoes in Crete.

### Mochlos — 2 hours 30
A tiny fishing village on the north-east coast with four tavernas on the water and a Minoan settlement on the islet fifty metres offshore, which was joined to the land in the Bronze Age. Nothing happens here, which is the point.

## Practical notes

- **Drive slowly.** Mountain roads are narrow, unfenced and shared with goats. Sound the horn on blind corners; everyone does.
- **Dress modestly** in churches and monasteries, Arkadi included. Shoulders and knees covered.
- **Buy from the village.** Olive oil, mountain herbs, honey, raki and textiles bought directly keep these crafts alive, and are cheaper and better than the equivalents on the coast.
- **Go in the morning or the evening.** Between one and five in summer, villages shut and sleep, and so should you.

faqs.q: What is the best village in Crete for pottery?
faqs.a: Margarites, 25 minutes from Rethymno. It is the centre of Cretan pottery, with over a dozen active studios and family workshops, and potters still throwing shapes descended from Minoan storage jars.

faqs.q: Are Cretan villages open to tourists in winter?
faqs.a: Yes. Inland villages stay open year-round, and winter is arguably their best season: fireplaces lit, slow-cooked food, local raki and no visitors. It is the coastal resorts, not the villages, that close.

faqs.q: Which Cretan villages can I reach without a car?
faqs.a: Very few directly. Buses to inland villages typically run once or twice a day and are timed for residents. Chora Sfakion and Loutro are the exception, reachable by coach and coastal ferry. For the rest, a guided village day with hotel pickup is the practical answer.

faqs.q: How many villages can I see in one day?
faqs.a: Three or four if they are clustered, such as Margarites, Eleftherna, Arkadi and Melidoni within half an hour of Rethymno. One or two if they are in different regions. Villages reward a long coffee, not a checklist.

faqs.q: Which village has the best food?
faqs.a: Archanes for restaurants and wine, Zaros for trout straight out of the spring water, Anogeia for meat and lyra, and Argyroupoli for eating under the plane trees with water running past your feet. Village food is seasonal and short-menued, which is why it is good.

faqs.q: Is it safe to drive to Cretan mountain villages?
faqs.a: Yes, if you drive slowly. Roads are narrow, often unfenced, and shared with goats. Sound the horn on blind corners, do not assume the oncoming vehicle will give way, and avoid driving unfamiliar mountain roads after dark.
